newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: FEDERAL MP BACKS EUTHANASIA
Federal Liberal MP, Chris Gallus, has called on all Federal politicians to understand the suffering a Darwin man endured in his final days before voluntary euthanasia was administered.

The man, in his mid-60s, who'd been suffering from prostate cancer, died at the weekend, becoming the first person to have his life terminated under voluntary euthanasia legislation, and the first in the world to die under such a law.
Ms Gallus is opposing a Private Member's Bill aimed at over-riding the Northern Territory's legislation.
She says before Federal MPs debate the bill, they should understand that the man was undergoing incredible suffering, with cancer through his body.
Ms Gallus says it was his choice to save himself some suffering, and die a little quicker than he otherwise would have.
AMA REMAINS OPPOSED TO EUTHANASIA
The Australian Medical Association says it still believes giving doctors legal authority to carry out mercy killing is a dangerous step for society.

Federal President Dr Keith Woollard says some members support mercy killing, but the AMA as a whole won't be changing its opposition to it even though the Northern Territory's law has been used to end a man's life.
He says the majority of doctors don't wish to have such authority.
Dr Woollard says it's not the AMA's role to act as a policeman but it's offering advice to the community on the sort of laws that should be in place.
DOWNER DEFENDS DALAI LAMA MEETING
Foreign Affairs Minister, Alexander Downer, has defended the Prime Minister's meeting with the Dalai Lama in Sydney later today, saying the Government must assert its independence.
Mr Downer may face criticism of the meeting when he meets Chinese officials tomorrow.
But he says the Prime Minister makes judgements about who he sees, not foreign governments, and Australians expect nothing less.
Meantime, Hollywood actor, Richard Gere, has praised John Howard for agreeing to meet the Tibetan spiritual leader in Sydney later today.
Richard Gere is known for his outspoken support of independence for Tibet and is also a financial supporter of the Dalai Lama.
IRVING CAN'T BE BANNED - KENNETT
The Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett says he doesn't agree with the views of British historian David Irving, but he doesn't know how he could be banned from visiting Australia.
Earlier this week, Mr Irving, who's declared the Nazi Holocaust did not happen, said he was preparing to lodge a fresh visa application.
He's making the move in the wake of the Prime Minister's comments about freedom of speech.
The Prime Minister, John Howard, describes Mr Irving as a crackpot, but says he won't reject out of hand his latest bid to visit Australia.
AFTERSHOCKS CONTINUE IN VICTORIA
Victoria is experiencing regular aftershocks from yesterday's earthquake.
Seismologists say aftershocks are occurring every five or ten minutes and may measure as high as the original five-point-two on the richter scale.
Director of the Seismology Research Centre, Gary Gibson, says aftershocks from a magnitude five-point-two earthquake typically last a few days, but their frequency this time is a little unusual.
EMPLOYERS PREDICT NO FAST JOBS GROWTH
A major employers' group has joined the new Reserve Bank governor in warning jobs are not likely to increase quickly under the Government's industrial relations reforms.

Governor of the Reserve Bank, Ian Macfarlane told the Economic Society's Conference of Economists in Canberra yesterday the changes to the employment landscape might have very little effect on job levels.

Executive director of the New South Wales Employer's Federation, Garry Brack, says two full economic cycles will be needed before it can be seen how the economy, business and unions respond to the Workplace Relations Bill.
He says the bill is good but not unblemished.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
